summary.title: Momompurin Live Manager — Application Threat Model (IAS Milestone 1)
summary.description: Threat model for the Phase 1 Android application: a Kotlin/Jetpack Compose client over a managed Supabase backend (PostgreSQL, GoTrue auth, object storage, PostgREST). Level 0 context and Level 1 decomposition with three trust boundaries and STRIDE threats embedded per element.

data.name:
Shop Owner
(Android device)
data.description: The business owner, authenticated on the Phase 1 Android app.

threats.title: T-01 Owner device compromised or credential stolen
threats.description: A lost or rooted device yields a live refresh token. Because the app is the only identity the business has, a stolen session is indistinguishable from the owner.
threats.mitigation: Device-bound refresh token, 30-minute access token, biometric unlock, and remote session revocation from the Supabase dashboard.

data.name:
Shop Owner
(Android device)
data.description: Single authenticated user of the Phase 1 application.

threats.title: T-01 Owner device compromised or credential stolen
threats.description: A lost or rooted device yields a live refresh token. Because the app is the only identity the business has, a stolen session is indistinguishable from the owner.
threats.mitigation: Device-bound refresh token, 30-minute access token, biometric unlock, and remote session revocation from the Supabase dashboard.

data.name:
1.0
Sign-In &
Session
data.description: Supabase Auth (GoTrue) client. Holds the JWT in EncryptedSharedPreferences.

threats.title: T-09 No durable audit trail of claim edits
threats.description: Claim rows can be overwritten with no record of who changed what. The owner cannot prove the state of a disputed order.
threats.mitigation: activity_log table written by trigger on every mutation, append-only, with actor id and before/after values.

data.name:
D1
Room (SQLite)
local cache
data.description: Offline-first local store for the live session. Holds customer PII until sync.

threats.title: T-08 Unencrypted Room database exposed via adb backup
threats.description: android:allowBackup defaults to true. A local backup extracts the SQLite file with every cached customer name, phone and address in plaintext.
threats.mitigation: allowBackup=false, dataExtractionRules denying cloud and device transfer, and SQLCipher on the Room database.

data.name:
2.0
Capture &
Validate Claim
data.description: Compose screen + ViewModel. Validates SKU, quantity and customer handle before write.

data.name:
3.0
PostgREST
API
data.description: Auto-generated REST surface. Executes every request as the role named in the JWT.

threats.title: T-05 Unbounded query on the auto-generated REST surface
threats.description: PostgREST honours Range headers and arbitrary filters. A single request can ask for the full order history, and there is no per-IP limit in front of the API.
threats.mitigation: Row limits in the client, a statement_timeout of 5s, and edge rate limiting of 60 requests/minute per token.

threats.title: T-02 Claim payload modified in transit or replayed
threats.description: The claim write trusts client-supplied quantity and price. A replayed or edited body can book stock at a stale price.
threats.mitigation: Price and stock are recomputed server-side in a Postgres function; the client sends SKU and quantity only; writes carry an idempotency key.

data.name:
4.0
Sync Worker
(WorkManager)
data.description: Background reconciliation of Room against Postgres after connectivity returns.

threats.title: T-03 Stale queued write overwrites a newer server row
threats.description: WorkManager retries a queued claim after connectivity returns. Without a version check the retry silently overwrites an edit the owner made on another device.
threats.mitigation: Optimistic concurrency on a row version column; conflicting writes are rejected and surfaced to the owner rather than merged silently.

data.name:
5.0
RLS Policy
Engine
data.description: Postgres row security. The only control that scopes an anon-key request.

threats.title: T-04 Row Level Security not enabled — anon reads every table
threats.description: The shipped schema granted SELECT to the anon role and never enabled RLS. The anon key is compiled into the APK, so any holder of the APK can read all customers, orders and supplier costs. Reproduced end to end in poc/run_poc.mjs.
threats.mitigation: Revoke anon grants, enable and force RLS on every table, attach an owner-only policy, and fail the CI build when any public table has relrowsecurity = false.

threats.title: T-06 Policy keyed on a client-controlled claim
threats.description: If the owner test reads user_metadata instead of app_metadata, the value is writable by the signed-in user and the policy authorises anyone who sets it.
threats.mitigation: Key every policy on app_metadata, which only the service role can write, and assert the claim name in the migration test suite.

data.name:
6.0
Invoice Edge
Function
data.description: Deno function that renders the invoice PDF and writes it to storage.

threats.title: T-10 service_role key reachable from the edge function
threats.description: The invoice function needs a service-role key to write storage. An unhandled error that echoes the environment returns that key to the caller.
threats.mitigation: Key injected as a Supabase secret, never read into a response, and a global error handler that returns a correlation id only.

data.name:
D2
PostgreSQL
customers · orders · inventory
data.description: Primary store for A-01, A-02, A-03.

data.name:
D3
Storage bucket
invoice PDFs
data.description: Object storage. Private bucket, signed URLs only.

threats.title: T-07 Public storage bucket enumerable by object name
threats.description: Invoice files named INV-0070.pdf in a public bucket are trivially enumerated, leaking customer names, addresses and order values.
threats.mitigation: Private bucket, RLS on storage.objects scoped to the owner, and 60-second signed URLs generated server-side.
